messages.content: I need to start planning Chicago for the academic publishing conference. The author dinner is Thursday at 7:00, setup begins Friday at 8:00, meetings run all day Saturday, and my last Sunday appointment ends at 11:30. I’ll be traveling alone from Denver and need flights plus three hotel nights downtown.

What are the conference dates, and where are the dinner and conference sessions being held? I’ll compare Thursday arrival margins, hotel totals, airport transfers, and Sunday flights that are realistic after the final appointment.
Thursday, March 12 through Sunday, March 15. The dinner is near Printer’s Row, and the conference is at the Hilton Chicago on South Michigan Avenue. I can stay elsewhere if it is an easy walk.

I found three workable structures at current quoted prices. Option A uses a nonstop DEN-ORD flight Thursday, 9:40 a.m.-1:10 p.m., and a Sunday nonstop at 4:05 p.m.; airfare is about $468. The Palmer House is $239 nightly, with an estimated three-night total of $846 after taxes. It is roughly a 15-minute walk from the Hilton and gives you a comfortable Thursday margin.
What does getting in from O’Hare do to that margin? I don’t want the scheduled arrival time treated as the hotel arrival time.

Allow about 75-105 minutes from landing to the Palmer House if you take the Blue Line and walk or transfer, including time to deplane. A taxi or rideshare can take 45-80 minutes depending on traffic. With a 1:10 p.m. landing, a reasonable hotel arrival range is 2:30-3:15. That leaves time to check in, regroup, and reach a 7:00 dinner even with a moderate flight delay.
Good. Give me a Midway version and one hotel closer to the conference so I can see whether either is materially better.

Option B is a DEN-MDW nonstop Thursday from 10:25 a.m. to 1:40 p.m., returning Sunday at 3:35 p.m., for about $512. The Hilton Chicago is quoting $274 nightly, approximately $969 for three nights after taxes. Midway to the hotel is commonly 35-55 minutes by Orange Line plus a short walk, or 30-60 minutes by car. You would likely reach the hotel around 2:40-3:15 Thursday and stay at the conference site.
That Sunday flight sounds tight. Walk me through it from an 11:30 finish.

For the 3:35 p.m. Midway flight, finish at 11:30, retrieve stored luggage by about 11:50, and leave the Hilton no later than 12:10. The airport trip could put you at Midway around 1:00, about two hours 35 minutes before departure. It works if the appointment ends on time, but the cushion shrinks quickly if the meeting runs over or traffic disrupts the transfer.
I would rather not spend Sunday watching the clock that closely. Is there a later Midway return?

There is a 5:25 p.m. nonstop from Midway at about $557 round trip. Leaving the Hilton around 1:15 after collecting your bag should put you at the airport roughly 2:00-2:20, giving more than three hours. That is operationally easier, though it costs about $89 more than Option A and gets you back to Denver later.
What is the third combination? Keep the full three-night cost visible, not just the nightly rate.

Option C pairs the 9:40 a.m. Thursday flight to O’Hare and the 4:05 p.m. Sunday return with the Congress Plaza Hotel, directly across from Grant Park. Airfare is about $468; the room is $189 nightly and approximately $673 total with taxes, making the combined flight-and-hotel estimate $1,141. The hotel is about a five-minute walk from the Hilton. The tradeoff is a more basic property and less consistent room feedback than the Palmer House.
And the combined estimates for the other two?

Option A, O’Hare flights plus Palmer House, is about $1,314 combined. Option B with the later 5:25 p.m. Midway return plus Hilton Chicago is about $1,526. Those figures exclude airport transportation, meals, baggage charges, and any destination or facility fee not shown in the quoted hotel totals.
Compare Sunday for O’Hare at 4:05 with the later Midway flight. Assume I leave the conference hotel after retrieving a checked bag from storage.

For O’Hare at 4:05, I would leave the Hilton area by 12:30. A car can range from about 45 to 90 minutes, while rail generally needs around 70-90 minutes with the downtown connection. That targets airport arrival between 1:30 and 2:00. The 5:25 Midway flight permits departure around 1:30-1:45 and still offers a solid buffer. Midway is less pressured; O’Hare remains credible if the meeting ends at 11:30 and luggage retrieval is prompt.
Could I stay at the Palmer House and still use Midway on Sunday, or does that make the transfer awkward?

That combination is straightforward. From the Palmer House, the Orange Line is accessible from the Loop, and a car to Midway is also practical. Pairing the Thursday O’Hare arrival, Palmer House, and Sunday 5:25 Midway departure would be about $1,403 before local transportation, assuming the mixed-airport airfare prices at roughly $557. It preserves the stronger Thursday flight timing and gives you the easier Sunday.
That seems like the best operational plan, but I want to know whether changing airports is buying enough to justify the higher fare.

The mixed-airport plan costs about $89 more than the O’Hare round trip. It buys roughly 80 extra minutes before departure Sunday and a shorter typical trip from downtown to the airport. You do not have a rental car to reposition, so the airport change adds little complexity. If the 11:30 appointment could overrun, that is a meaningful margin; if it is firm, the 4:05 O’Hare flight is still reasonable.

Keep Palmer House. The Hilton premium is not worth it, and I don’t want the uncertainty of the Congress Plaza for a work weekend. Check whether a slightly later O’Hare nonstop keeps the fare below the mixed-airport version.

A 5:30 p.m. O’Hare nonstop is currently pricing at about $534 round trip. With the Palmer House estimated at $846, the combined total is about $1,380. That is around $23 below the mixed-airport plan and gives you an extra 85 minutes over the 4:05 flight. Leaving the Hilton around 1:00-1:15 after bag collection should provide a credible airport margin.

Use that as the leading combination. Before anything is issued, have the office verify the hotel total and cancellation terms, luggage storage Sunday, and whether there is an unused airline credit that can be applied. I also want the exact flight numbers and fare rules checked.

Leading plan: fly nonstop Denver to O’Hare Thursday morning, scheduled 9:40 a.m.-1:10 p.m.; stay three nights at the Palmer House, checking out Sunday; and return nonstop from O’Hare at 5:30 p.m. after the 11:30 appointment. Current estimates are $534 airfare, $846 lodging, and $1,380 combined before transfers and incidental charges. The office should verify exact flight numbers, operating carriers, fare rules, seat and bag charges, schedule-change terms, and application of any unused airline credit before ticketing. It should also confirm the Palmer House room type, itemized three-night total, mandatory fees, deposit and cancellation deadline, Thursday check-in, and Sunday luggage storage. Hold the 4:05 O’Hare and 5:25 Midway combinations only as comparison fallbacks until the later O’Hare itinerary is verified.
